segments.text: What do you do when your agent makes a
mistake? Do you get angry? Do you get
frustrated? Or do you think, "How do I
make that mistake harder for the agent
to make next time?" And so, the question
becomes, "Okay, what mechanisms do I
have to achieve that?" Well, you have
the retro skill. This is a skill that's
fresh in my skills repo for v1.3. And
what it does is it conducts a
retrospective on your previous sessions.
So, if a mistake happens in your
previous sessions, you run retro, and it
will do a retrospective, and it will try
to find the mistakes, try to find the
inefficiencies in your process, and turn
them into either automated checks that
deterministically check that your agent
is doing the right thing, or it will add
them into steering files like coding
standards.md to make sure that code
review agents catch those mistakes
before they go to production. Retro has
been absolutely invaluable for me. It's
really forced me to consider that maybe
my code base is not as good as I thought
it was. And I really recommend you give
it a go cuz it's surprising what your
agents will put up with without moaning.
And retro gives them an outlet to
actually improve the code base that they
operate in.
